Spacing

A consistent spacing scale from 0 to 12 (plus 16, 20, 24, 28, 32) applied with margin and padding utilities in any direction.

Visual Scale

The spacing scale is based on a 0.25rem (4px) base. Each step increments by 4px until 1rem, then scales up for larger gaps.

Spacing scale
css 
--zak-space-0:   0;
--zak-space-0-5: 0.125rem;  /* 2px  */
--zak-space-1:   0.25rem;   /* 4px  */
--zak-space-1-5: 0.375rem;  /* 6px  */
--zak-space-2:   0.5rem;    /* 8px  */
--zak-space-3:   0.75rem;   /* 12px */
--zak-space-4:   1rem;      /* 16px */
--zak-space-5:   1.25rem;   /* 20px */
--zak-space-6:   1.5rem;    /* 24px */
--zak-space-8:   2rem;      /* 32px */
--zak-space-10:  2.5rem;    /* 40px */
--zak-space-12:  3rem;      /* 48px */
--zak-space-16:  4rem;      /* 64px */

Margin

Apply margin in all directions, horizontal (mx), vertical (my), or individually with mt, mr, mb, ml.

Margin utilities
zak-m-4
(inside)
Container with .zak-p-2 (8px padding)
zak-mx-auto (centered)
css 
/* All directions */
.zak-m-0  .zak-m-1  .zak-m-2  .zak-m-3  .zak-m-4  .zak-m-5
.zak-m-6  .zak-m-8  .zak-m-10 .zak-m-12 .zak-m-auto

/* Individual sides */
.zak-mt-0 .zak-mt-1 .zak-mt-2 .zak-mt-3 .zak-mt-4 .zak-mt-5  /* top */
.zak-mr-0 .zak-mr-1 .zak-mr-2 .zak-mr-3 .zak-mr-4 .zak-mr-5  /* right */
.zak-mb-0 .zak-mb-1 .zak-mb-2 .zak-mb-3 .zak-mb-4 .zak-mb-5  /* bottom */
.zak-ml-0 .zak-ml-1 .zak-ml-2 .zak-ml-3 .zak-ml-4 .zak-ml-5  /* left */

/* Axis */
.zak-mx-0 .zak-mx-1 ... .zak-mx-5 .zak-mx-auto  /* left + right */
.zak-my-0 .zak-my-1 ... .zak-my-5 .zak-my-auto  /* top + bottom */

Padding

Padding utilities mirror the margin system with a p prefix.

Padding utilities
p-1 (4px)
p-2 (8px)
p-3 (12px)
p-4 (16px)
p-5 (20px)
css 
/* All directions */
.zak-p-0 .zak-p-1 .zak-p-2 .zak-p-3 .zak-p-4 .zak-p-5
.zak-p-6 .zak-p-8 .zak-p-10 .zak-p-12

/* Individual sides */
.zak-pt-0 ... .zak-pt-8   /* top    */
.zak-pr-0 ... .zak-pr-6   /* right  */
.zak-pb-0 ... .zak-pb-8   /* bottom */
.zak-pl-0 ... .zak-pl-6   /* left   */

/* Axis */
.zak-px-0 ... .zak-px-8   /* left + right */
.zak-py-0 ... .zak-py-8   /* top + bottom */

Auto

Use auto margins to center elements along an axis.

Auto margins
mx-auto
my-auto
html 
<!-- Center horizontally -->
<div class="zak-mx-auto" style="width:120px;">block</div>

<!-- Center vertically (needs a flex container) -->
<div class="zak-d-flex">
  <div class="zak-my-auto">item</div>
</div>

::available: .zak-m-auto .zak-mx-auto .zak-my-auto .zak-mt-auto
            .zak-mr-auto .zak-mb-auto .zak-ml-auto

Negative Margin

Pull elements outward with negative margin utilities. These use a m prefix followed by the size (e.g. m-n3 = -0.75rem).

Negative margins
Parent container
ml-n4 (-16px)
Common for creating full-bleed or overlapping layouts.
css 
/* Overlap an element outside the parent, e.g. -16px */
.zak-ml-n4 { margin-left: -1rem; }
.zak-mt-n3 { margin-top: -0.75rem; }

/* Common negative utilities:
   .zak-m-n1 ... .zak-m-n5
   .zak-mx-n1 ... .zak-mx-n5
   .zak-my-n1 ... .zak-my-n5
   .zak-mt-n1 ... .zak-mt-n5
   .zak-mb-n1 ... .zak-mb-n5
   .zak-ml-n1 ... .zak-ml-n5
   .zak-mr-n1 ... .zak-mr-n5 */

Accessibility

  • Prefer spacing utilities over adding extra empty elements — it keeps the document structure clean for assistive technology.
  • Use auto margins and flexible layouts instead of hard-coded pixel offsets where possible.
  • Negative margins can cause content to overflow; ensure adequate spacing so focus or text is never clipped.
  • Maintain a consistent spatial rhythm (e.g. 8px grid) to reduce cognitive load and improve scanability.
